keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria drops the Twente and Achterhoek strip only in 1600; the page dates 'Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597'. The Battle of Nieuwpoort (1600) 'yielded a Dutch tactical victory without durable strategic gains'. The shape also adds two cells on the Tuscan coast (Livorno province) that no page opened explains (unverified: page budget). Repair pass: the two Livorno-province cells are on Elba (10.21-10.43 E, 42.8 N, checked with the gazetteer), where the Spanish held Porto Longone. The State of the Presidi page says only 'Construction of Fort San Giacomo at Porto Longone began in March 1605' and gives no year for the Spanish presence; the Porto Azzurro page says Appiani 'granted Spain the right to build a fortress there' in 1557 and that the town was transferred to the State of the Presidi, also without an acquisition year. Neither page confirms nor refutes Cliopatria's 1600 start (the 1557 grant suggests the cells could be earlier); kept as drawn, unverified. Neither page mentions Finale; the Italian dominions have no event in this dossier.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1602 shape (1602-1608) holds five cells in County Cork (51.7-52.0 N, 8.5-8.8 W, the Kinsale district) and two cells on Bahrain. Siege of Kinsale page: infobox span '2 October 1601 - 3 January 1602'; the Spanish 'gave up the town to Mountjoy and were allowed to sail back to Spain', on terms that they be 'conveyed back to Spain on giving up their other garrisons of Dunboy, Baltimore, and Castlehaven'; the page does not say any Spanish troops stayed, so no Spanish ground remains from 1602 and the Cork cells are removed (the 1601 expedition was never drawn: the 1600 shape ends in 1601). History of Bahrain: 'the Portuguese remained in control until they were driven out of the island in 1602', so Bahrain is removed from 1602 (ledger event of 1602). Ostend (West Flanders) is added from 1604 (next keyframe) on the Eighty Years' War page's 'Spain recorded successes at the Siege of Ostend (1601-1604)'.

The Palatinate cells Cliopatria drops in 1632 and restores in 1636 are not explained by any page opened (the Thirty Years' War page is silent on a Swedish conquest of the Rhine; unverified: page budget). The infobox gives 'War of the Portuguese Succession: 25 August 1580' and 'Union period 1580-1640'; Philip 'was recognized as king by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581'. ledger.note: 1582 (bridging, confidence 1): the union inherits the war with the Republic. The page's infobox dates the war 'c. 1566/1568 - 30 January 1648' and the Dutch Republic's Cliopatria shape starts in 1582; the page does not date the first Spanish campaign of the union's years. Repair pass: the reviewer would date the union's inheritance of the war to 1580, but the compile has no opposing state before 1582 (the dutch-republic dossier starts in 1582; the Act of Abjuration is 26 July 1581 per its notes), so a contest zone drawn from 1580 would border nothing; the war itself is dated 1568-1648 in the wars entry.

ledger.note: July 1582: the fight for the Azores. The page places the naval battle 'off Terceira Island on July 26, 1582' and a second 'off São Miguel Island on July 27, 1582', and says the navy's victory 'resulted in the rapid conquest of the Azores'; ground fighting on Terceira is not described.
1583: António's attempt to rule from Terceira 'came to an end in 1583'. The page gives no month and no detail of the last resistance.
1583: the Azores pass to Philip II, completing the Portuguese Succession war. Cliopatria's shapes already include part of the islands in 1582; see the 1582 keyframe.

1585: Parma retakes Flanders and Brabant. 'Parma's reconquests more or less stalled after the Fall of Antwerp (1585)'. The page names no other city and dates no other recapture; the Fall of Antwerp page says only that 'most of the County of Flanders and the Duchy of Brabant had been recaptured in the preceding year', a year it does not name, so 1585 (the Antwerp year) is the latest date for Ghent, Brussels and the rest of the block. Cliopatria's union shape adds these cells only in 1588 (this is the Belgian part of the 66-cell 1588 delta: 12 cells, about 3,000 km2, against 54 cells for the north-east gain); the new keyframe iberian-union_1585 draws them from 1585. Mirror: dutch-republic /ledger/1 and habsburg-netherlands /ledger/16.

ledger.note: 1588 (bridging, confidence 1): the north-east of the Netherlands is drawn Spanish. The page is silent on the dates of the Spanish gains: 'Many of these territories had been previously lost to the Spanish in the 1580s'; Parma's campaign brought 'ever more provinces and cities in the southern, eastern and northeastern parts of the Netherlands back into royalist hands.' The Siege of Zutphen (1591) page gives a lower bound for two towns: 'In 1586, the English under the Earl of Leicester took Zutphen's important outlying sconce', then 'English turncoat Rowland York handed the sconce over to the Spaniards' and 'William Stanley handed over the nearby town of Deventer to the Spaniards' (neither handover is dated), so Zutphen and Deventer passed to Spain after 1586; the page is silent on the other towns. The Flemish and Brabant cells that Cliopatria adds in the same shape are now the two 1585 gains above (repair pass, 2026-10-31). The Dutch recaptures of 1590-1597 below are dated by the Eighty Years' War page.

ledger.note: 1590: the Dutch take Breda. 'Maurice and William Louis subsequently captured Breda in 1590'; Geertruidenberg followed 'in 1593'.
1591: the Dutch take Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl and Nijmegen: 'Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, and Nijmegen in 1591'. The radii are the researcher's.
1592: the Dutch take Steenwijk and Coevorden: 'Steenwijk and Coevorden in 1592'.

1594: the Dutch take Groningen: 'Groningen in 1594'. The page names the city; the province and the rest of the north-east (Friesland, Drenthe), which Cliopatria drops in the same step, are the researcher's reading.
1597: the Dutch take Grol (Groenlo), Enschede, Ootmarsum and Oldenzaal: 'and Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597'. Cliopatria's shape drops this strip only in 1600.

1601: the siege of Ostend begins. 'Spain recorded successes at the Siege of Ostend (1601-1604)'; the page gives no more; the Battle of Nieuwpoort (1600) 'yielded a Dutch tactical victory without durable strategic gains'.
1601: the court moves from Madrid to Valladolid: 'transferred to Valladolid, with the whole administrative staff'; destination in identity.capitals.

1602: Bahrain is lost to Persia. History of Bahrain: 'the Portuguese remained in control until they were driven out of the island in 1602'; 'The power vacuum that resulted was almost immediately filled by the Persian ruler, Shah Abbas I'. Cliopatria keeps two Bahrain cells in the union shape to 1608; the keyframes from 1602 remove them. The safavid-dynasty dossier has the matching 1602 gain (its counterpart there is portuguese-empire).
1604: the siege of Ostend ends in a Spanish success (the page gives no result beyond 'successes').
1604: Ostend, the Republic's foothold on the Flemish coast, is Spanish again. The page does not say the town was taken; Cliopatria adds its cells only in 1609.
1606: the court returns to Madrid (the end of the page's 1601-1606 span; the return itself is the researcher's reading).

1606 (confidence 2): Spinola's campaign brings Oldenzaal and Groenlo back under Spain. Page: 'Spain recorded successes at the Siege of Ostend (1601-1604) and during Spinola's campaign of 1605-1606' (no place named). The Ambrogio Spinola page names the captures, with no year in the sentence: 'his campaign resulting in capturing Oldenzaal, Lingen, Wachtendonk, Groenlo and Rheinberg for the Spanish'; Lingen, Wachtendonk and Rheinberg lie outside the drawn lands. The Dutch conquer Oldenzaal in 1626 and Groenlo in 1627 (events below), so Spain held them again; 1606, the end of the campaign, is the year used because the pages date neither fort. Cliopatria's union shapes of 1600-1636 hold no cell within 12 km of either fort (checked with the gazetteer), so the keyframes from 1606 add them. Mirror: habsburg-netherlands /ledger/23 (the same two forts); dutch-republic /ledger/12 draws a larger Overijssel and Gelderland loss from its own Cliopatria cells.

notes:
Iberian Union (Cliopatria 1582-1639). Pages opened for this state: the five of the budget (Iberian Union, War of the Portuguese Succession, Eighty Years' War, Thirty Years' War, Franco-Spanish War) plus the Reapers' War page, which was opened for the catalonia dossier and is cited once here for the 1640 split.

What the Cliopatria row is: not Iberia alone but the whole European monarchy of the Spanish Habsburgs: Spain, Portugal, the Italian dominions (Naples, Sicily, Sardinia, Milan), the Low Countries and Franche-Comte, plus Madeira, part of the Azores, Muscat and (to 1608) Bahrain. The kingdom-of-spain and kingdom-of-portugal dossiers (eu-12) record the merge into this union in 1580/1581 and the split on 1 December 1640; the Low Countries are also drawn by the habsburg-netherlands dossier (1482-1795, eu-09), so the compiler must give those cells to one state in 1580-1640. My keyframes keep them (the Iberian Union page lists the 'Council of Flanders' territories as part of the union); if the compiler gives them to habsburg-netherlands, remove the Low Countries cells from my keyframes and drop the Dutch-front events (they duplicate dutch-republic and habsburg-netherlands events).

Start and end: the infobox gives the union 1580-1640; Cliopatria 1582-1639. I used 25 August 1580 and 1 December 1640 and added keyframes for 1580, 1581 and 1640. For 1640 the successors' Cliopatria shapes (Spain, Portugal, Catalonia) already cover the lands; the compiler should let them win.

Disagreements and gaps: (1) The Thirty Years' War page dates the Spanish occupation of the Lower Palatinate to October 1619 and, in the same page, says that by November 1622 most of it was held; the electoral-palatinate dossier has 1621-1622 from its own page. Cliopatria draws the Palatinate only from 1622. (2) The Palatinate cells dropped in 1632 and restored in 1636, the northern France band (kept to 1639 by Cliopatria, a 1636 incursion on the page), the Cork cell 1602-1608, Bahrain to 1608, the Livorno cells from 1600 and Muscat to 1639 have no page behind them: 'unverified: page budget'. A gap-filler should open: Battle of Kinsale, Portuguese Bahrain, Portuguese Oman/Muscat, Swedish phase of the Thirty Years' War, Electoral Palatinate. (3) The Cliopatria shapes show Spanish gains in the north-east of the Netherlands in 1588 but the pages give no date for them (confidence 1; the Siege of Zutphen page puts Zutphen and Deventer after 1586). The Belgian cells of the same shape are dated 1585 (repair pass). (4) The kingdom-of-france dossier names kingdom-of-spain as its counterpart for 1636; until 1639 the Cliopatria row is this union. (5) No infobox area on the Iberian Union page, so no area comparison was possible; Cliopatria's 797,000-814,000 km2 includes the Low Countries and Italy.

Overseas: the Dutch conquests in Brazil (Recife and Olinda in 1630), Elmina, Luanda and Ceylon, and the loss of Hormuz, are on the Iberian Union page but outside the Cliopatria shape (they belong to the portuguese-empire and spanish-empire rows); no events recorded here.

Region names the gazetteer lacks (coordinates used instead): Zutphen, Deventer, Nijmegen, Delfzijl, Steenwijk, Coevorden, Groenlo, Enschede, Ootmarsum, Oldenzaal, Venlo, Roermond, Breda, Ostend, Corbie.

Repair pass, 2026-10-31 (author, after the review): (a) Palatinate occupation start 1620 (reviewer's fix kept). (b) Parma's reconquest: new gains of 1585 (Antwerp, 17 August; Flanders and Brabant) and the new keyframe iberian-union_1585; the 1588 gain is the north-east only. (c) Spinola's campaign: gain of 1606 (Oldenzaal, Groenlo), keyframes from 1606 and a 1625-1628 split for the 1626 and 1627 losses; the reviewer thought Cliopatria's 1609 shape re-adds Twente and Achterhoek cells, but the gazetteer shows no cell within 12 km of either fort in any shape of 1600-1636, so the keyframes add the two forts themselves. (d) Venlo and Roermond retaken in 1637. (e) Cork cells (Kinsale, ended 3 January 1602) and Bahrain (lost 1602) removed from the shape from 1602, with a 1602 Bahrain loss to safavid-dynasty. (f) Not resolved: the Low Countries are still drawn by both this dossier and habsburg-netherlands (orchestrator decision; if habsburg-netherlands keeps them, drop the Dutch-front events and subtract the Low Countries from the keyframes: ledger events with counterpart dutch-republic, the 1585, 1606 and 1625-1627 keyframes and the Belgian part of every shape); the Palatinate gap of 1632-1635 (pages silent); the Elba cells (pages silent on the year); the Italian dominions (no event; Finale page not opened).
